449-about-atmospheric-and-oceanic-scienc: Physics, applied math and sometimes chemistry applied to meteorology, climate and air quality, using quantitative models. Studied both through fluid mechanics (winds, currents, circulation) and detailed processes (clouds, sea ice, heat exchange). Upper-level courses are often 500-level and need math or physics.
449-location: Burnside Hall, Room 305, 805 Sherbrooke St. W. Adviser: David Straub.
449-program-description: The basics of the atmosphere and ocean, weather and climate.
449-complementary-courses-18-credits: 9–15 from the first list, 3–9 from the second. ATOC 219 or CHEM 219, ATOC 404 or PHYS 404, not both.
451-biology: Foundation science may not meet all medical or dental requirements. Meet each program adviser regularly, and your Science adviser about degree requirements.
451-about-biology: Life from molecules to ecosystems: evolution, environment, development, cells, inheritance, disease and the nervous system, applied in agriculture, medicine, biotechnology and conservation.

Liberal, Major, joint majors with Computer Science and Mathematics, Honours, Joint Honours with Computer Science, Minor, Science for Arts, Quantitative Biology options, and B.A. & Sc. concentrations (p. 453).
Leads to jobs and professional schools in medicine, veterinary, dentistry, agriculture, nursing, education and library science, or to research.

Stewart Biology, Bellini and Duff buildings, with links to Redpath Museum, MUHC, the Neuro, the Sheldon Biotechnology Institute and the Smithsonian in Panama. Field courses at Gault Nature Reserve, Barbados, Panama and East Africa. U2 and U3 students can do research for credit. MBSU represents students.
451-preprogram-requirements: Major and Honours: two courses each of elementary biology, general chemistry and math, plus one or two of physics. B.A. & Sc., Liberal and Minor: same except physics varies. Foundation science may not meet medical or dental requirements. Joint and Quantitative students should see the Undergraduate Adviser.
452-biology-concentrations: Guidelines only, not requirements. Complementaries must be at 300+, and 200-level ones are electives. Check rules for courses outside Arts and Science. Develop computing skills for advanced study. Key courses are listed by discipline.
453-location: Stewart Biology Building, Room N7/9B, 1205 Dr. Penfield Ave. Adviser: Nancy Nelson.
453-program-description: B.A. & Sc. only: a broad introduction to cell and molecular biology. Choose this or Organismal, not both; the Major goes deeper. 18–19 credits, depending on CHEM 212.
454-required-courses-13-credits: Required courses taken elsewhere without credit are replaced by approved complementaries, for at least 18 in all. With CHEM 212's equivalent, take another approved course.
454-complementary-courses-6-credits: Biology at 300+, approved by the Adviser.
454-required-courses-16-credits: Same replacement rule, at least 18 credits in all.
454-program-description-2: A basic grounding from molecules and cells to organisms and ecosystems, including development, behaviour and evolution. Foundation students: some courses need PHYS 101 or 102.
455-complementary-courses-18-credits: 3–4 CHEM (with CHEM 212 credit, CHEM 204, 222 or 300–500 Biology with approval), 3–4, 3 and 3 from three lists, 4–6 Biology at 300–500.
456-chemistry: The B.A. & Sc. Major isn't certified by the Ordre des Chimistes; for a Québec chemistry career, take a B.Sc. Foundation science may not meet medical or dental requirements.
456-about-chemistry: Understanding atoms and molecules to predict how matter and energy change, basic to biology, medicine and geology.
Leads to industry research, quality control, government labs, medicine, an MBA, or patent law and forensic work.
Four areas: organic, inorganic, analytical, physical, plus polymer, theoretical, green, nano and biological in upper years. Most courses have labs. Honours, Major, Liberal and other programs.
456-office-for-science-and-society: Promotes critical thinking and accurate science for the public, media and students, with presentations and "The World of Chemistry" courses.
456-location: Otto Maass Building, Room 322, 801 Sherbrooke St. W. Advisory Office: Room 116.
456-program-description: A grounding in chemistry through one traditional sub-discipline.
456-required-courses-13-credits: If part of your main program or taken at CEGEP, substitute from the options list; at least 19 credits exclusive to the minor.
457-program-description: Restricted to B.A. & Sc. and B.Sc./B.Ed. Not certified by the Ordre des Chimistes.
457-required-courses-21-credits: Courses taken elsewhere without credit are replaced from the list at equal value, for at least 36 in all.
458-about-cognitive-science: Intelligent behaviour in humans, animals and machines, through Computer Science, Linguistics, Neuroscience, Philosophy and Psychology, using a computational view of mind. Interfaculty and Honours programs.
458-program-description: B.A. & Sc. only: extends the Interfaculty program with a research project. See the Adviser first. Program GPA 3.3 at graduation, B+ or better in COGS 444, and an approved minor. At least 21 credits each in Arts and Science.
459-complementary-courses-30-credits: 18 from one list, 12 from any, with 15 at 400+.
459-linguistics: Any LING at 300–500, or the list.
